newsitem.title: USA: GM shifts commercial trucks to Flint, Mich..
newsitem.headline: GM shifts commercial trucks to Flint, Mich..

text.p: General Motors Corp said Friday it will invest about $500 million in its Flint, Mich., truck assembly plant to prepare it for production of GM's full range of commercial trucks and a derivative of the company's next generation full-size C/K pickup truck.
As part of the investment, GM said it will shift commercial and medium-duty truck production to Flint from two other plants, in Detroit and Janesville, Wis.

GM said it will close the 78-year-old Detroit P-Chassis plant, which builds truck chassis for recreational vehicles, school buses and specialty vans, during the year 2000. Production of those products will be moved to Flint.
GM also said will move production of medium-duty commercial trucks to Flint from Janesville in 2001.
However, Janesville will continue to be GM's lead plant for full-size sport/utility vehicles, and will build next generation versions of GM's Tahoe, Yukon and Suburban models.
The moves are desinged to increase GM's overall capacity for both medium-duty commercial and light duty trucks.
GM said the consolidation of commercial truck production in Flint will bring cost savings and will help it sharpen its focus on developing better products for the commercial truck market.

"The optimization of our facilities will allow us to reduce our structural costs, make better use of our resources, and improve our productivity," said Ned McClurg, general manager of the GM Powertrain Group.
GM's investment plan for the Flint plant calls for the company to construct two new body shops, a second paint shop and additional chassis, trim and general assembly lines.
The plant will continue to operate on a two-shift production schedule.

On a more near-term schedule, GM said about 90 truck engineers associated with P-Chassis production will move from the Detroit plant earmarked for closure to GM's new Truck Product Center in Pontiac. The Truck Product Center and related facilities, opened last year, now handle all engineering and product development work for GM trucks.
